task: Horizon 13 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project (roadmap rev2 after a second REPLAN): add viewport-default and single-element (CDP clip rect, element addressed by a findElement CSS-locator ref) screenshots to the standalone tools/chrome-bridge tool, extending the existing captureTab action in place across the parity surface with a flat too-large result-size guard, closed by a mandatory live-Chrome head-to-head verification. Full-page (captureBeyondViewport) capture was dropped in rev1 after a phase-0 probe proved it non-functional on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab. Rev2: the rev1 verification attempt found the shipped size-guard ceiling (600_000) sits below the real ~845KB viewport base64 and so breaks the default viewport capture, that server.ts never surfaces the width/height metadata the cross-check needs, and that an un-scrolled below-the-fold element captures blank on the unfocused tab (h10 render-pass suspension) - so a corrective phase is added and the verification phase is narrowed to an element scrolled into view first, with un-scrolled below-the-fold capture deferred behind the same render-the-tab prerequisite full-page sits behind.

analysis.objective: Ship one more browser-control capability in the standalone tools/chrome-bridge tool - viewport-default and single-element (CSS-locator-ref-addressed, CDP clip-rect) screenshots of the dedicated unfocused sandbox tab - across the established parity surface with the too-large size guard calibrated to the real measured viewport size and the returned image dimensions surfaced to the MCP client, closed by a mandatory live-Chrome verification. Full-page / beyond-viewport capture is out of this horizon (phase-0 probe 2026-09-04: non-functional on the unfocused tab). Single-element capture targets an element scrolled into view first: the unfocused sandbox tab does not paint off-viewport content (h10 render-pass suspension), so reliable un-scrolled below-the-fold element capture is deferred behind the same render-the-tab prerequisite.
analysis.successDefinition: Done means all of the following hold: (1) the screenshot capability lets a caller request a capture of a single element addressed by the same CSS-locator ref shape findElement returns, with the existing viewport-only behaviour preserved as the default AND that default capture no longer wrongly rejected by the size guard; element capture targets an element scrolled into view first (via the shipped scrollPage action) - reliable un-scrolled below-the-fold element capture is NOT in this horizon because the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab paints no off-viewport content (h10 render-pass suspension; live 2026-09-04 a never-scrolled element captured blank, reproduced twice), and full-page / beyond-viewport capture is NOT in this horizon (the live phase-0 probe on 2026-09-04 proved Page.captureScreenshot({captureBeyondViewport:true}) hangs past the 15s withDebuggerSession cap or errors CDP -32000 on the unfocused sandbox tab and never returns an image); (2) the change lands consistently across every parity-surface member the recent horizons touch - the per-action Params/Result interfaces in protocol/types.ts, both Record<PageAction, ...> mapped types, the raw + guarded handler maps in extension/page-actions.ts, the TOOL_CATALOG entry in mcp/tool-catalog.ts, the affected unit tests, and the README prose/manual-e2e step - with no drift (a missing consumer is a tsc error), and PAGE_ACTIONS stays at 20 (the shape changes in place, not via a new action); (3) failure shapes are explicit and non-throwing where the precedent is non-throwing: element selector matches nothing, element has zero/na box, relay/tab unavailable, and an over-large image are each defined result outcomes, not unhandled hangs or crashes; (4) the returned image stays within MCP result-size limits via a documented flat too-large guard carrying measured bytes plus a named ceiling constant calibrated ABOVE the real measured default viewport base64 (~845KB / 844960 chars measured live 2026-09-04 at dpr 2, not the stale ~275KB h4 figure - a ceiling below it breaks the default capture), and the result carries width/height/clipped metadata that mcp/server.ts actually surfaces to the client (an added text content block alongside the image block) so it can be cross-checked; (5) no new manifest permission is added (debugger is already granted); (6) npm run verify for the tools/chrome-bridge package is green (tsc --noEmit, eslint --max-warnings 0, vitest) and boky's own extension/bridge/verify pipeline is untouched; (7) a MANDATORY live head-to-head runs in a fresh post-rebuild MCP session covering both the default viewport capture (returns an image, not a too-large outcome) and a real large element scrolled into view first (via scrollPage), the element image dimensions cross-checked against a CDP evaluatePage getBoundingClientRect measurement (devicePixelRatio reconciled) per the horizon-12 precedent, the default capture's measured base64 size recorded under the recalibrated ceiling (the rev1 too-large regression gone; the guard's fire path stays unit-test-covered since every capture path this horizon ships is viewport-bounded), a clean post-run debugger-detach check, and a recorded note that un-scrolled below-the-fold capture is deferred behind the render-the-tab prerequisite - all in a dated Verified README block; an honest MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING note is an acceptable close if the live environment is unavailable, a hand-waved pass is not.
assumptions: The slice is delivered by extending the existing captureTab capability in place - CaptureTabParams gains a required-with-default two-value mode field (visible viewport | element) and an elementRef field, CaptureTabResult gains width/height/clipped and a too-large marker - keeping PAGE_ACTIONS at 20, mirroring the h12 decision that a result/param shape may change in place rather than via a new action.

The element is addressed by the same self-contained CSS-locator string findElement/clickElement already accept (h12 decision) - never a CDP backend node id, opaque handle, XPath, or index into a prior result set.

Element capture uses CDP Page.captureScreenshot({ clip: { x, y, width, height, scale } }) with the element rect measured via the post-h9 CDP read path (evaluatePage / Runtime.evaluate getBoundingClientRect); this stays within the h6 decision that CDP is used only for the captureVisibleTab-family gap via Page.captureScreenshot.
The capture reuses per-command withDebuggerSession attach/detach (15s cap) with no persistent CDP session, consistent with the h10 scroll decision.

The result is still returned as a data:image/png;base64,... dataUrl surfaced to MCP as an image content block for a real capture, and as a text/error block for a structured non-image outcome (too-large / element-not-found / zero-area).
Verification is Claude-Code-only (h4 decision), live signed-in Chrome, in a fresh MCP session started after the extension rebuild + reload.

The phase-0 probe (rev0) already proved the ref->clip resolution and clip mechanism are correct on the unfocused sandbox tab; the rev1 verification attempt then proved the one-off 'clip composites a below-the-fold element' probe result was NOT steady-state (a never-scrolled element captures blank because the unfocused tab paints no off-viewport content - h10), so element capture in this horizon targets an element scrolled into view first via the shipped scrollPage action.

The rev1-shipped MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS = 600_000 is below the real default viewport base64 (844960 chars measured live 2026-09-04 at dpr 2), so the corrective phase raises it to 1_200_000 (real measurement + headroom) and keeps the guard flat; the ceiling is a code constant, not a value re-derived at runtime.

mcp/server.ts's successful-capture branch currently emits only the image content block; the corrective phase adds a sibling text content block carrying { captured, width, height, clipped } so an MCP client can read the returned image's pixel dimensions for the cross-check.
risks: A ceiling set below the real default viewport base64 breaks the default capture (the rev1 bug - 600_000 vs the real ~845KB); the corrective phase's answer is a flat ceiling at the real measurement plus headroom (1_200_000). Because every capture path this horizon ships is viewport-bounded (default viewport, or an in-view element clip cropped to the viewport), the guard cannot fire on a real capture in this horizon - its too-large branch stays covered by unit tests, and live-observing it fire is not a close criterion.

Large-image CDP encode of a big element clip may approach the 15s withDebuggerSession cap; the per-command attach/detach lifecycle and timeout must still clean up (the h10 hang + orphaned-attachment failure is the precedent to avoid).

Element capture needs a bbox-measurement round-trip before the capture; a per-command detach between the measure session and the capture session can race scroll position or lifecycle state, yielding a clipped or offset image.

clip interacts with device-scale-factor / emulation overrides - the returned image may not match measured CSS-pixel dimensions unless devicePixelRatio (2 on the sandbox tab) is reconciled explicitly, weakening the mandatory cross-check.

Live verification is repeatedly blocked in this project by relay-down or a frozen MCP tool catalog (h9, h11, h12); the horizon may again end MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and need a --retry in a later fresh session.

An element selector that matches nothing, matches a display:none / zero-area node, or matches an off-screen node needs a defined non-throwing outcome; picking error vs a structured {captured:false}-style result inconsistently with the codebase's existing non-throwing precedents is a latent inconsistency.

discoveryFindings.finding: In src/extension/page-actions.ts the raw handler was `captureTab: async () => { const tabId = await sandboxTab.resolveTabId(); const dataUrl = await captureDebugger.captureScreenshot(tabId); return { result: { dataUrl } }; }` wrapped as `captureTab: guard(raw.captureTab)`. discoveryFindings.finding: TOOL_CATALOG.captureTab in src/mcp/tool-catalog.ts was `{ description: '...Takes no arguments.', inputSchema: NO_ARGS }`. The rev0 probe shim replaced NO_ARGS with a two-property schema. listTools() derives the advertised list and order from PAGE_ACTIONS, not Object.keys(TOOL_CATALOG).

discoveryFindings.finding: src/mcp/server.ts handleToolCall special-cases `if (toolName === 'captureTab') return imageResult(stripDataUrlPrefix(readDataUrl(response.result)))`. imageResult returns `{ content: [{ type:'image', data: base64Png, mimeType:'image/png' }] }`. Every other tool returns textResult(JSON.stringify(result,null,2)). Errors -> textResult(..., true) with isError:true. No size/base64 guard here. readDataUrl returns '' on a shapeless result.
discoveryFindings.implication: The `=== 'captureTab'` branch must be generalised: a real capture still renders as an image block, but a structured too-large / element-not-found / zero-area outcome is detected before the imageResult path and surfaced via textResult with isError set as appropriate; server.unit.test.ts gets coverage for each non-image outcome plus the success case.

discoveryFindings.finding: Signature `withDebuggerSession<T>(tabId: number, label: 'capturing' | 'evaluating' | 'scrolling', run: () => Promise<T>, timeoutMs = CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<T>`. The label union is a closed 3-member string-literal union. CDP_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000. It attaches chrome.debugger '1.3', races run() vs a detach rejection and a timeout, and in finally clears the timeout, deletes the inFlight entry, then detaches (catch noop). One chrome.debugger.onDetach listener registered at construction.
discoveryFindings.implication: The element-rect read and the clip screenshot reuse existing labels ('evaluating' / 'capturing') or add a label literal to this union and its test; the 15s cap and attach/detach lifecycle come for free.

discoveryFindings.finding: In screenshotTab: `await chrome.debugger.sendCommand({tabId}, 'Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' })`. Only format:'png' is passed. Reply parsed by readScreenshotBase64. debugger-ports.unit.test.ts pins the call: `toHaveBeenCalledWith({tabId:7},'Page.captureScreenshot',{format:'png'})`. The rev0 probe shim added an options arg forwarding captureBeyondViewport + clip.
discoveryFindings.implication: Element = add clip:{x,y,width,height,scale}; the captureBeyondViewport branch from the probe shim is removed. DebuggerPorts.captureScreenshot(tabId, options?): Promise<string> keeps an optional options arg for clip only. The pinned unit-test assertion must keep asserting the viewport call sends exactly {format:'png'}.

discoveryFindings.finding: DebuggerPorts.evaluate(tabId, expression): Promise<InPageScriptOutcome> in debugger-ports.ts calls Runtime.evaluate `{ expression, returnByValue:true, awaitPromise:true }` mapped via cdpEvalOutcome to {ok:true,json}/{ok:false,error}. The port already does internal geometry reads: private readScrollMetrics evaluates `({ scrollY, scrollHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight, innerHeight, innerWidth })` via the same shape.
discoveryFindings.implication: Measuring an element getBoundingClientRect() is directly doable - reuse public evaluate() or add a private helper mirroring readScrollMetrics/parseScrollMetrics. No new CDP domain. ref->rect resolution runs as a Runtime.evaluate returning the rect JSON.

discoveryFindings.finding: The ref CSS-locator is generated inside the ISOLATED-world injected function in raw.findElement (page-actions.ts ~line 498) by buildRef(el, depth): prefers `#${CSS.escape(id)}` when unique, else recurses up building `${buildRef(parent)} > ${tag}:nth-of-type(${index})`, capped at MAX_REF_DEPTH = 8. clickElement consumes any selector via document.querySelector(selector). findElement re-feeds a ref through document.querySelectorAll(selector).
discoveryFindings.implication: Element-screenshot-by-ref can resolve the rect with document.querySelector(ref).getBoundingClientRect() via CDP evaluate exactly as clickElement/findElement do - no new ref format or handle registry.

phases.name: Add viewport and element capture modes to captureTab
phases.goal: In one atomic change across the captureTab parity surface, add a mutually-exclusive two-value mode field (visible viewport | one element by ref) plus an element-ref field, resolve the ref to a CDP clip rect via the existing Runtime.evaluate read path, return width/height/clipped metadata in the result, and add a flat non-throwing guard that turns an oversized returned image into a defined too-large outcome. Full-page / captureBeyondViewport is not in scope (phase-0 probe proved it hangs past the 15s cap or errors CDP -32000 on the unfocused sandbox tab and never returns an image).
phases.rationale: captureTab today takes no arguments and captures only the visible area, and nothing anywhere checks screenshot size. The phase-0 probe proved clip-rect capture composites a genuinely below-the-fold element (table.wikitable at y=4459.77, scrollY 0) on the unfocused sandbox tab in 2058ms with a clean detach, while captureBeyondViewport:true is non-functional there.
